summary:
cmcr-70172 1.1.0 (Double vision, dizziness and progressive leg weakness · 9-year-old boy) teaches paediatric Wernicke encephalopathy outside the alcohol setting: recognising it at the bedside, giving injected thiamine before any glucose and before the scan, keeping the mimics honest (MFS/GBS, encephalitis, myasthenia, Bickerstaff/ADEM), refeeding safely, and stating an unmeasured diagnosis as clinical. An earlier attempt had left a partial case.json draft (the README was still 1.0.0); I reviewed it line by line against the 1.0.0 fact base, continued from it, and fixed its errors.

PHASES (static clock, none learner-switchable): admission (6 days into the illness: history from the relative plus the boy's own words, exam, bedside glucose/weight and bloods) → workup (MRI, CSF and neostigmine records; opens after objectives 1–3 and decisions 1–2) → first-week (opens only once injected thiamine is given and the work-up is interpreted) → one-month (outcome; waits for all 5 decisions; the figure appears only here).

DECISIONS (5, 4–5 options each, own feedback naming guidance, no length cue in either language): bedside-diagnosis (Wernicke encephalopathy, probably with neuropathy, treated now vs MFS→IVIG, continue the encephalitis treatment, myasthenia, Bickerstaff/ADEM steroids); thiamine-regimen (injected treatment dose before glucose, weigh him, do not wait for a level vs oral tablets, level first, glucose drip first); workup-interpretation (supports it, but an early normal CSF cannot exclude GBS vs Leigh→stop vitamins, CVT→anticoagulate, everything excluded, unproven without a level); feeding-safety (K/Mg/P checked and repeated, swallow screen, gradual build-up with the dietitian vs rapid catch-up, a week nil by mouth on glucose, normal diet now); outlook (clinical diagnosis, continue thiamine, find the cause, follow up vs stop and discharge, colectomy explains all, it was GBS after all).

INTERVENTIONS (13): IV access with a pre-dose sample, injected thiamine, oral thiamine, glucose-containing drip, saline, mannitol, aciclovir, IVIG, swallow screen, dietitian, neuro obs, surgical/GI review, neurology follow-up. glucose-infusion is critical:true (contraindicated before injected thiamine). thiamine-oral and IVIG are critical:false (contraindicated before injected thiamine). No doseSpec, because no fixed dose is stated (weight and the report's dose are unrecorded). A bare "thiamine" is now ambiguous, so the learner must say the route.

RUBRIC (13 items; 28 deterministic points + 1 examiner-judged communication item): critical items are rb-thiamine-early (an act done in time: {intervened thiamine-iv, whenIndicated}, window = MRI not yet read) and rb-no-glucose-first (avoided harm, with scoredWhen). I added rb-no-early-alternatives (safety, non-critical), because oral-first and IVIG-first cost nothing before. Decisions are scored first-try.

MEASURED SCORES (core assess, 2026-11-14): reference 28/28 (100 %), safety passed; do nothing 0 (0/23 counted); wrong first answer at every decision 16/28 (57 %); glucose drip before thiamine 25/28 (89 %) with the safety outcome FAILED; oral-only thiamine first 26/28; IVIG first 26/28; thiamine only after the MRI 24/28 with the critical item missed; the course before admission continued 24/28; every dangerous act plus wrong first answers 11/28 with safety FAILED.

STAFF: Dr Ren (attending: Socratic, debriefs with PEARLS, revealsDiagnosis false), Nurse Bai (ISBAR handover), Dr Xu (radiologist), Pharmacist Qin.

DEBRIEF: 6 teaching points, 5 dated and attributed (EFNS 2010, Zuccoli & Pipitone 2009, EAN/PNS 2023, ABN/BPAIIG 2012, ASPEN 2020); 7 Vancouver references with verified DOIs. 57 test utterances (29 zh / 28 en, 5 negatives).

README.md is rewritten with all 16 parts, including the measured-score table, the Safety outcome paragraph, the To-verify list, the 1.1.0/1.0.0 changelog and the 中文摘要 with 安全结果.

Every 1.0.0 fact (88ed0d2 case.json + README) and where it sits in 1.1.0:

F1 Age 9, male → patient.age/sex; title; triage note.
F2 Dizzy, sees double, legs getting weaker (presentation) → history presentation, double-vision (the boy speaks), dizziness (the boy speaks), leg-weakness; chiefComplaint.
F3 "已经6天" (six days) → presentation; phase label "six days into the illness".
F4 Treatment did not help; increasingly listless (没精神) and somnolent (嗜睡); unable to walk → prior-treatment, drowsiness, leg-weakness; exam ex-alertness and ex-gait (history-derived, labelled in their sources).
F5 Vomited once a day in the week before onset; does not like meat → vomiting-week, diet.
F6 Part of the colon removed for intestinal atresia on day 4 of life → neonatal-surgery.
F7 Mannitol and antiviral medicines used → prior-medicines (antiviral unnamed, no doses); mannitol and aciclovir interventions, whose responses note the earlier use.
F8 Three days of treatment as encephalitis at another hospital, no relief → prior-treatment.
F9 Intermittent vomiting since the surgery → vomiting-chronic.
F10 1.0.0's unknown items (past illnesses, allergies, family, exposures, function, red flags, worries) → unknown history items allergies, family, fever-infection, swallowing, bowel-habit, growth, leg-sensation, regular-medicines, glucose-fluids; the worries are a labelled role (concerns).
F11 Bilateral ptosis → ex-eyelids. Restricted adduction/abduction with horizontal and vertical nystagmus → ex-eye-movements.
F12 Leg power III, knee reflexes not elicited, calf tenderness, pathological signs negative → ex-leg-power, ex-reflexes, ex-calves.
F13 Gag slightly weak; finger–nose steady and accurate → ex-gag, ex-coordination.
F14 MRI: symmetrical thalamic, lentiform and fornix signal, FLAIR high, lentiform DWI slightly high → mri (workup).
F15 CSF routine and biochemistry normal → csf. Blood count and muscle enzymes no obvious abnormality → blood-count, muscle-enzymes (timing unrecorded, placed at admission, labelled).
F16 Neostigmine test negative → neostigmine-test.
F17 Recurrent vomiting and selective eating (nutritional record) → vomiting-chronic, diet; D4 prompt.
F18 Quantitative vitamin B1 testing unavailable → thiamine-level (available:false with the recorded text).
F19 Vitamin B1 given (dose, route, duration unrecorded) → thiamine-iv response; week1-course; outcome.
F20 One week after B1: diplopia, dizziness and eye movements improved; walked a few metres → week1-course, status-week1, ex-eye-movements-week1, ex-gait-week1.
F21 At one month: leg power V, MRI reported normal → ex-leg-power-month1, mri (one-month), status-month1, outcome.
F22 The article's diagnosis (title): vitamin B1 deficiency encephalopathy → debrief, README.
F23 1.0.0's unknowns (level, intake, absorption, long-term cognition) → unknowns (expanded to 7).
F24 Figure fig01 (approved; sha256 a7da6df5…) → assets; attached to the outcome record only.
F25 Source: DOI 10.3760/cma.j.issn.1673-4912.2014.03.028 and URL → provenance and references.

CONTRADICTIONS KEPT (README "Source and adaptation" and To verify):
(1) One-week outcome: zh "1周" vs en "within a week" → "by one week"; both readings named.
(2) "生化": zh is CSF biochemistry; en "Routine CSF/biochemistry" could mean blood → zh followed; blood biochemistry stays unknown.
(3) Vomiting: zh "每天吐一次" (once a day) vs en "daily" → zh kept.
(4) "不爱吃肉" vs en "avoids meat" → "does not like meat".
(5) Whether the one-month MRI counts from the B1 or from admission → "at one month".

INFERENCES (derived, not new): vomiting "for years" / "since infancy" (day 4 of life to age 9); the meaning of the power grades; a "probable" thiamine-deficiency neuropathy (weak legs, absent knee reflexes, calf tenderness; no NCS recorded); the one-month MRI being a repeat; the dietary-deficiency criterion "likely but unmeasured"; the colectomy's role "unproven".

STAYS UNKNOWN: weight, height and growth; vital signs and GCS; glucose, electrolytes, gas and lactate; CSF and blood values; the B1 dose, route and duration; fluids and whether they held glucose; the antiviral's name and both doses; how encephalitis was diagnosed elsewhere; NCS, anti-ganglioside antibodies, CSF virology; upper-limb power, sensation, ankle reflexes, pupils, fundi; allergies, family history, infection, swallowing, bowels, leg pain; the extent of the resection (small bowel?); the cause of the vomiting; anything after one month; which relative accompanied him.
safetyFixes: Replaced 1.0.0's management key, which only 'assessed' thiamine, with injected thiamine at a treatment dose given at the bedside before any glucose and before the MRI. The act is scored in time by the critical item rb-thiamine-early ({intervened, whenIndicated}; the window closes when the MRI is read), replacing 1.0.0's hindsight critical item, a decision answered after reading the outcome.

A glucose-containing drip before injected thiamine is contraindicated and critical:true: it fails the safety outcome and the critical item rb-no-glucose-first. The harm text keeps the hypoglycaemia caveat ('never withhold glucose if low; give thiamine first or alongside'), replacing 1.0.0's caricature distractor 'always withhold life-saving glucose'.
Added rb-no-early-alternatives (safety, non-critical): oral-only thiamine first and IVIG first were flagged as contraindicated in the draft but cost no marks.

Made the thiamine route explicit in the matcher: a bare 'thiamine'/'维生素B1' now ties between the injected and oral items, so the learner is asked for the route instead of being credited automatically with the injected route.

Removed facts the draft had invented in teaching text: 'a child who does not drink / has never drunk alcohol' (alcohol is not recorded), 'he is vomiting' (present tense) and 'eating little', 'lost weight', 'no meat'/'不吃肉', 'restricted diet', 'day by day'. Neuropathy is now 'probable', and 'areflexia' used as a patient fact is now 'absent knee reflexes'.

Removed attributions that could not be verified: 'continue thiamine until no further improvement' attributed to EFNS 2010 (not confirmable), the EFNS statement on addressing the cause, and a Caine-criteria count that overstated the dietary-deficiency criterion (now: two signs recorded, the third likely but unmeasured). The ASPEN refeeding key now says his risk cannot be graded without a weight or intake, so treat him as at risk.

The thiamine dose text no longer implies a fixed duration. No paediatric mg dose is printed: weight is unrecorded, so the dose is calculated by weight and age with the pharmacist, and there is no doseSpec.
guidelines: Galvin R et al. EFNS guidelines for diagnosis, therapy and prevention of Wernicke encephalopathy. Eur J Neurol 2010;17(12):1408-18, doi:10.1111/j.1468-1331.2010.03153.x. Checked online: all 9 abstract recommendations read via Europe PMC (suspect WE in any condition leading to deficiency; two of four signs in alcoholics; blood thiamine sampled before the first dose; MRI to support the diagnosis in both groups; 200 mg three times daily, preferably IV, before carbohydrate).

da Silva JSV et al. ASPEN consensus recommendations for refeeding syndrome. Nutr Clin Pract 2020;35(2):178-95, doi:10.1002/ncp.10474. Checked online: Europe PMC record; paediatric statements (thiamine 2 mg/kg, max 100–200 mg/d, before feeding or dextrose; K/Mg/P before feeding and every 12 h for 3 days if high risk; start at 40–50 % of goal) confirmed via secondary summaries (BAPEN 2024 guidance, WikEM). The full text was not reachable; the case uses only the qualitative steps.

van Doorn PA et al. EAN/PNS guideline on diagnosis and treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome. Eur J Neurol 2023;30(12):3646-74, doi:10.1111/ene.16073. Checked online (abstract): IVIG 0.4 g/kg for 5 days within 2 weeks if unable to walk unaided; electrodiagnostic testing advised; anti-GQ1b testing when MFS is suspected.

Kneen R et al. ABN/BPAIIG national guidelines: management of suspected viral encephalitis in children. J Infect 2012;64(5):449-77, doi:10.1016/j.jinf.2011.11.013. Checked online via the Encephalitis Society synopsis: aciclovir can be stopped in an immunocompetent child once an alternative diagnosis is made (B, III); transfer to a paediatric neurology unit if failing to improve.

Zuccoli G, Pipitone N. Neuroimaging findings in acute Wernicke's encephalopathy. AJR 2009;192(2):501-8, doi:10.2214/AJR.07.3959. Checked online: typical sites; atypical sites reported in non-alcoholic patients (Zuccoli AJNR 2009; a 2010 letter disputes how sharp the difference is).

Sechi G, Serra A. Wernicke's encephalopathy: new clinical settings and recent advances in diagnosis and management. Lancet Neurol 2007;6(5):442-55, doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(07)70104-7. DOI checked online (Europe PMC).
Source article: 张波 et al. 小儿维生素B1缺乏性脑病一例. 中国小儿急救医学 2014;21(3):193-4, doi:10.3760/cma.j.issn.1673-4912.2014.03.028. Verified in the source map (publisher check 2026-10-29).
toVerify: Source pass: every fact against the full article, especially the one-week outcome (zh '1周' vs en 'within a week'), whether '生化' is CSF or blood biochemistry, the vomiting frequency, which eye(s) had restricted adduction/abduction, the MRI wording and timing, whether the MRI, CSF and neostigmine test came before or after vitamin B1, the B1 dose and route, the antiviral's name, the extent of the neonatal resection (colon only, or small bowel too), anything after one month, and what fig01 shows (to give it a precise title).
EFNS 2010 full text: its wording on treatment duration and on children. The case states no duration and no longer names Caine.

ASPEN 2020 full text: the paediatric thiamine (2 mg/kg, max 100–200 mg/d), monitoring (K/Mg/P every 12 h × 3 days) and energy-start (40–50 % of goal) statements, which were confirmed only via secondary summaries, and its paediatric risk criteria.
EAN/PNS 2023 full text: the wording on CSF protein being normal early in GBS.
Zuccoli & Pipitone 2009: the phrasing that atypical sites are reported 'mainly in patients without alcohol use' (the AJNR series supports it; a 2010 letter disputes it).

Clinician review: a paediatric neurologist to confirm the bedside key (treat as WE before the scan), the critical status of a glucose drip before thiamine, and the decision not to print a paediatric thiamine dose; a paediatric dietitian to review the refeeding key.
